issues.title: Session without context manager usage
issues.description: The rule requires all database sessions to use 'with Session(db.engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:' pattern for proper resource management, but the code creates a session without a context manager and never closes it
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
session = Session(db.engine)
row = session.scalar(stmt)
if not row:
    raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
session.commit()
issues.rule_name: SQLAlchemy Sessions Must Use Context Managers

issues.title: Database transaction commits called on every variable update instead of batched
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer now calls flush() inside the loop for each updated conversation variable, rather than batching all updates and flushing once after the loop completes. This causes multiple unnecessary database commits when multiple conversation variables are updated in a single node execution, significantly degrading performance and creating database contention. The original implementation correctly tracked whether any updates occurred with the `updated_any` flag and only flushed once after all updates were queued.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence layer registered before persistence layer causing event ordering issue
issues.description: The conversation_variable_layer is now registered before the persistence_layer in the graph engine layer stack. In event-driven architectures with layered middleware, the order of layer registration determines the order in which layers receive and process events. By registering conversation_variable_layer first, it will receive and process NodeRunSucceededEvent events before the persistence_layer has a chance to persist the node execution state. This creates a race condition where conversation variables might be updated in the database before the corresponding node execution is persisted, leading to data inconsistency if failures occur between the two operations.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence failures are silently ignored
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer calls update() without catching exceptions, relying on the graph engine's blanket exception handler which logs but continues execution. When persistence fails (e.g., database errors, ConversationVariableNotFoundError), the exception is caught by the engine's try-except in event_manager.py, logged, and execution continues. This creates silent data loss where the in-memory variable pool contains updated values but the database doesn't, causing data inconsistency. In the original implementation, these errors would fail the node execution and stop the workflow, providing clear feedback to users.

issues.title: ConversationVariable query missing tenant_id filter
issues.description: The SELECT against the tenant-scoped ConversationVariable table is filtered by id and conversation_id only, with no tenant_id predicate. This violates the requirement that tenant-scoped queries must include tenant_id scoping to prevent cross-tenant data access.
issues.rule_name: Database Queries Must Include tenant_id Scoping

issues.title: Missing return type annotation on __init__
issues.description: The __init__ method is missing an explicit return type annotation (e.g., "-> None"), which violates the requirement that all Python function definitions include type annotations for parameters and return values.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: def __init__(self, variables: dict[tuple[str, str], object] | None = None):
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30531 - feat: Add conversation variable persistence layer

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves conversation-variable persistence out of the Variable Assigner nodes (v1 and v2) and into a new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`. The layer watches `NodeRunSucceededEvent`s for assigner nodes, reads the `__updated_variables` process data, looks each variable up in the runtime variable pool, and writes it through `ConversationVariableUpdater`. The DB implementation moves from `core.workflow.nodes.variable_assigner.common.impl` to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, and the import-linter exemption for it is removed. `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` now takes a selector sequence.

The direction is good: it pulls DB I/O out of the workflow core. The new path does change behavior in three ways that matter, though:
- **Session leak:** the moved updater no longer closes its SQLAlchemy session.
- **Stale values inside iterations:** the layer reads the value from the *parent* engine's variable pool. Inside an Iteration node, that pool hasn't been synced from the per-iteration copy when the event is handled, so the last assignment in an iteration can be lost.
- **Silent failures:** persistence errors now go through the engine's layer-exception handler, which logs them and lets the run succeed. Before, the node failed.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Two bugs should block merge: the updater leaks a DB session/connection on every write, and conversation variables assigned inside Iteration nodes can be persisted with stale values. Error handling also became silent.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, each Variable Assigner node (v1/v2) wrote conversation variables straight to the database through `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl`, which lived inside `core.workflow.nodes` and imported `extensions.ext_database`. The node also recorded the changed selectors in `process_data['__updated_variables']`.

After this PR, nodes only change the in-memory `VariablePool` and emit `process_data`. The advanced-chat app runner registers a new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` on the `GraphEngine`. The `EventManager` passes every engine event to its layers. The new layer filters for assigner success events, looks up each updated conversation variable in the engine's `ReadOnlyVariablePool`, and calls the updater, which now lives in `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`. Layer exceptions are caught and logged by `EventManager._notify_layers`.
steps: Start at `AdvancedChatAppRunner.run` (core/app/apps/advanced_chat/app_runner.py). It now builds `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer(conversation_variable_updater_factory())` and registers it before the workflow persistence layer.
The Variable Assigner nodes (v1/v2 `node.py`) no longer touch the DB. They update `variable_pool` and return `NodeRunResult.process_data` with `__updated_variables`.
The worker puts node events on the queue. The dispatcher hands them to `EventManager.collect`, which calls `_notify_layers` and swallows any layer exceptions.

`ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer.on_event` filters for VARIABLE_ASSIGNER success events and reads `sys.conversation_id`. For each `conversation.*` selector, it reads the variable from the read-only pool and calls `update` and `flush`.
`services/conversation_variable_updater.py` holds the moved DB implementation. `ConversationService` also uses it for API-driven variable edits.
`ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` / `ReadOnlyVariablePoolWrapper.get` now take a selector sequence instead of `(node_id, key)`.

findings.title: Updater leaks a SQLAlchemy session (and pooled connection) on every update
findings.body:
During the move, `with Session(db.engine) as session:` was replaced by a bare `session = Session(db.engine)`, and the session is never closed:

::diff{file="api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py" lines="14-23"}

When the row isn't found, `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` is raised while a transaction is open. On success, `commit()` runs but the session object stays alive until GC. Either way the connection isn't returned to the pool deterministically.

This runs once per updated conversation variable on every chatflow assigner execution. It also runs on the `ConversationService.update_conversation_variable` API path. Under load this can exhaust the pool (`QueuePool limit ... overflow` timeouts).

::suggestion{file="api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py" lines="18-23"}
        with Session(db.engine) as session:
            row = session.scalar(stmt)
            if not row:
                raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
            row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
            session.commit()
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` (lines 14-23) creates `Session(db.engine)` without closing it, which leaks connections on both the success and not-found paths. Restore the `with Session(db.engine) as session:` context manager from the original `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py`, keeping the new `ConversationVariableNotFoundError`. Consider adding a unit test confirming the session is closed when the row is missing.

findings.title: Assignments inside Iteration nodes can be persisted with stale values
findings.body:
The layer ignores the `new_value` already carried in the event's `process_data`. Instead it reads the variable from the variable pool of the engine the layer is attached to:

::diff{file="api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="45-53"}

That is the top-level engine. `IterationNode._create_graph_engine` gives each iteration a **deep copy** of the pool (`variable_pool.model_copy(deep=True)`), and the assigner inside the iteration writes to that copy. The child's `NodeRunSucceededEvent` is re-yielded through the iteration node into the parent engine, so this layer does see it. But the parent pool is only updated afterwards, by `_sync_conversation_variables_from_snapshot`, after the iteration's events have been yielded (sequential path at iteration_node.py ~L203-214; parallel path ~L277-285).

Example: conv var `x=0`, a sequential iteration over 2 items, and an assigner `x = x + 1` inside:
- Iteration 0: the layer reads parent `x=0`, then sync sets it to 1.
- Iteration 1: the layer reads parent `x=1`, then sync sets it to 2.
- Result: the DB ends at `1` while the in-memory value is `2`. The final assignment is lost.

Worker and dispatcher are different threads, so the outcome is also non-deterministic. The old code didn't have this problem because the node persisted the `Variable` from its own pool.

::callout{type="warning"}
The unit tests use a mocked read-only pool that already holds the updated value, so they can't catch this.

A fix is to build the persisted variable from the event payload: take `id`, `name`, and `selector` from the pool entry (they don't change), and take `value` from `item.new_value`. For example: `variable.model_copy(update={'value': item.new_value})`, or rebuild it via `variable_factory` using `item.value_type`. Another option is for the node to put the full serialized variable in process_data.
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` (lines 38-53), the layer persists the value read from the top-level `graph_runtime_state.variable_pool`. Assigner nodes inside an Iteration node write to a deep-copied pool (`iteration_node.py` `_create_graph_engine`), and that copy is synced back only after the iteration's events are emitted, so the layer persists stale values. Change the layer to persist the value carried in the event (`UpdatedVariable.new_value`/`value_type` from `process_data`). Use the pool lookup only for identity fields (id, name, selector, description). Add a test where the pool holds an older value than the event's `new_value` and assert the event's value is what gets persisted.

findings.title: Persistence failures are now silently swallowed; the run still reports success
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` `on_event` (lines 22-53), DB errors from `ConversationVariableUpdater.update` propagate to `EventManager._notify_layers`, which only logs them. The workflow then succeeds while the variable isn't persisted, and one failing variable stops the rest of the loop. Wrap each item's update in try/except that logs selector + conversation_id with `logger.exception` and continues. Decide whether failures should also surface to the run, for example by recording them and raising or aborting in `on_graph_end`. Also log a warning when `conversation_id` is None but conversation variables were updated. Add tests for an updater that raises.

findings.title: `flush()` called per variable inside the loop instead of once per event
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` line 53, `flush()` is called inside the per-variable loop. Move it after the loop and call it once, only if at least one `update` was issued, matching the old v2 node behavior and the batching contract in `core/workflow/conversation_variable_updater.py`. Update the unit tests accordingly.

findings.title: Redundant `__init__` added to v2 VariableAssignerNode
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py` lines 56-68, remove the `__init__` that only calls `super().__init__`, and remove the now-unused `TYPE_CHECKING` imports (lines 25-27). Also update the docstring of `ConversationVariableUpdater` in `api/core/workflow/conversation_variable_updater.py`: it is now consumed by `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`, and a single instance is shared per graph run.

findings.title: Good layering: DB access removed from workflow nodes
findings.body: Moving `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl` into `services/` lets the `core.workflow.nodes.variable_assigner.common.impl -> extensions.ext_database` import-linter exemption be deleted. The assigner nodes are now pure in-memory transforms, which makes them much easier to test. The updated v1 tests check the observable `__updated_variables` output instead of mock call counts. Fixing the `ReadOnlyVariablePool.get` signature so it matches the real `VariablePool.get(selector)` is also a nice consistency improvement.
